iran_school_claim.finding: Substantially true. On Feb 28, 2026 — the opening day of the US-Israeli war on Iran — a US strike (CENTCOM, reportedly two Tomahawk missiles) destroyed the Shajareh Tayyebeh elementary school in Minab, southeastern Iran, ~25 km from the Strait of Hormuz, inside a walled compound adjoining an IRGC base. '123' is the number of CHILDREN killed as identified by Airwars (all aged 13 or younger), confirmed by Bloomberg's investigation ('at least 123 children'). The total death toll is higher: Airwars 157 (123 children + 34 adults incl. 26 staff and 5 parents), range 157-168; Iranian state media 168; UN fact-finding mission >150 incl. 120 children; Reuters/BBC/WaPo (Mar 15) 156 incl. 120 schoolchildren. Early Feb 28 reports attributed it to Israel; the IDF said it found no link, and subsequent US-official and AP/Bloomberg reporting attribute it to a US missile. The Pentagon has not formally accepted blame; a CENTCOM-commissioned investigation is unpublished, a Pentagon review reportedly blamed Palantir's Maven Smart System AI targeting and the lapse of no-strike-list updates after Hegseth cut the Civilian Protection Center of Excellence, and in Oct 2026 Hegseth's advisers reportedly planned to withhold the report until after the Nov 3 midterms. Not confirmed from any primary CENTCOM document.
